title: Mail each waiting notification exactly once

blocks.text: The notification service collects what happens to each user during the day (a paid invoice, a failed build, a new comment) and a digest job mails each user what is waiting for them, in one message, every few minutes. Request threads keep adding notifications while the job runs. Support has two kinds of ticket: users who never got a notification the admin page showed as waiting, and users who got the same build failure in two digests in a row.

`DigestOutbox` already collects notifications. Write `sendDigests(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/DigestOutbox.java`: mail every user who has something waiting, one message each, and return how many users it mailed.
When you're done, every notification reaches its user exactly once, in the run that was going on when it arrived or in the next one, whatever arrives during a run. About six lines in total.
The tests run the job on one thread and add notifications from inside the mailer, which is where a request thread's add lands in production.

cases.says: with nothing arriving during the run, each user gets one message with all their waiting notifications, and nothing is left waiting
a run with nothing waiting sends no message
a notification added for a user the run has already mailed reaches that user once, by the next run
a notification added for a user while that user's message is being sent is not lost
when a notification arrives during a user's send, the next run mails only the new one, not the ones already sent

origin.section: A Concurrent Add Is Seen or Missed by Where It Lands, So Walking and Then Clearing Loses Writes

concepts: Walking a concurrent map or queue and then calling clear() loses what arrived during and after the walk; taking each element out with remove(key) or poll() loses nothing.
